subject: Meteorology
title: Wind Shear and Storm Structure
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wind Shear and Storm Structure.

hook.text: Wind shear sounds destructive—but it's actually what organizes supercells into long-lived, structured monsters.

buildup.text: Speed shear (wind getting faster with height) tilts the updraft, moving rain away from the storm's inflow.

discovery.text: Directional shear (wind changing direction with height) creates horizontal spinning—like rolling a pencil.

twist.text: The updraft tilts this horizontal spin into the vertical—producing the mesocyclone that defines a supercell.

climax.text: Without shear, you get ordinary storms that die quickly. With shear, storms organize and intensify.

punchline.text: Shear is the sculptor that shapes a storm into a supercell.

quiz.question: How does directional wind shear contribute to supercell formation?
options: It creates horizontal rotation that gets tilted into the vertical
